key_insight: Aligning the reference image's latent representation with the diffusion model's internal representation (instead of adding auxiliary cross-modal features) yields more faithful, consistent and controllable reference-to-video generation.
problem_solved: Existing R2V methods fuse extra high-level or cross-modal signals with VAE latents, causing representation mismatch, suboptimal conditioning, and reduced fidelity/temporal coherence in generated videos.
method: Representation alignment: map the reference image VAE latent into the diffusion Transformer's native latent space so conditioning is consistent and directly usable.
Integrated conditioning: inject the aligned reference representation into the DiT conditioning pathway (no separate auxiliary feature streams), simplifying architecture and improving feature fusion.
Training objectives: combine reconstruction/denoising losses with an alignment loss (and temporal-consistency regularizer) to preserve appearance while enforcing stable dynamics across frames.
impact: Makes reference-to-video synthesis more reliable and easier to deploy by improving visual fidelity, temporal coherence, and conditioning simplicity — beneficial for personalized content, virtual try-on, and controllable video generation pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing VAE latent -> alignment module -> DiT conditioning (contrast with prior multi-stream fusion design).
Before/after comparison frames: original reference image, video from baseline fusion method, video from aligned-representation method.
Attention / feature-alignment visualization: similarity maps showing better correspondence between reference and generated frames.
Temporal-consistency chart: frame-wise identity/LPIPS or qualitative coherence illustrations across time.
paper_title: RefAlign: Representation Alignment for Reference-to-Video Generation
paper_authors: Lei Wang, YuXin Song, Ge Wu, Haocheng Feng, Hang Zhou
